text: Why does an 8-bit signed type run from -128 to 127 rather than -127 to 127?
choices: One of the 256 patterns is spent on zero, leaving 255 to split, and 255 is odd
It is an arbitrary decision made by the language designers
Because the sign bit cannot represent positive 128
Because 128 is a power of two and 127 is not
explanation: 256 patterns, one used for zero, leaves 255 for non-zero values — an odd number, which cannot split evenly. Zero is grouped with the positives, so there are 127 positives and 128 negatives. The asymmetry is arithmetic, not a design whim.
